newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends down as call money rate falls.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends down as call money rate falls.

text.p: * Central Bank sells more than $100 million to curb peso fall
The Philippine peso ended sharply down at 26.265 as banks bought dollars following a fall in the overnight money and Treasury bill rates, traders said.
The sharp decline was stopped by Central Bank after it started selling dollars at 26.265 to tame the fall.
"Banks and customers decided to cover their position as they saw the interest rate differentials between peso and dollar instruments narrowed down," one trader said.

Domestic interest rates fell after banks swamped the T-bill auction following the restrictions set by the Central Bank on the purchase of termed reverse repos. Rates went down by about 50 basis points in all maturities.
The Bank decided to waive the secrecy of the transaction, allowing the Bureau of Internal REvenue to monitor sales of reverse repos.
The peso opened weaker at 26.213 as against 26.211 at Friday's close.
Turnover amounted to $283.7 million, of which $100 million were sold by Central Bank. - RAMONCITO DELA CRUZ 63 2 8418938
